channel.title: HotNews — China, every day.
channel.description: Daily stories about China in technology, finance, sports, entertainment, lifestyle, science, travel and culture — for readers around the world.

item.title: China's Auto Industry Faces a Wave of New Models and Deals
item.description: A busy week in China's car market brought nine new model launches, a major restructuring between two state-owned automakers, and a shift in the Huawei-Seres partnership, signaling intensifying competition and consolidation.

item.title: China's Auto Repair Talent Gap Grows as EV Boom Accelerates
item.description: China's electric vehicle boom is creating a shortage of skilled repair technicians, with salaries doubling but positions still unfilled. The WorldSkills competition in Shanghai highlights the advanced skills needed for modern vehicles.

item.title: China's Electric Car Repair Shops Can't Find Enough Workers
item.description: As electric vehicles flood Chinese roads, repair shops are struggling to hire technicians who understand both mechanics and software. At the WorldSkills competition in Shanghai, young mechanics showed why the job now demands programming skills.

item.title: China's EV Repair Shortage: Double the Pay, Still No Takers
item.description: As electric vehicles flood Chinese roads, a severe shortage of qualified repair technicians is emerging. Fixing an EV now demands mechanical, electrical and software skills — and training pipelines are struggling to keep up.

item.title: One Day, Nine New Cars: Inside China's Crowded EV Market
item.description: On September 23, nine new models from brands like Geely, Changan and Denza hit Chinese showrooms in a single day. The pile-up reflects brutal competition in the world's largest car market, where too many models chase too few buyers.

item.title: Booker Prize 2026 Shortlist Unveiled, Celebrating Writing AI Cannot Copy
item.description: The 2026 Booker Prize shortlist, announced in London, features six novels from four countries, including two past winners and three first-time nominees. Chair of judges Mary Beard calls the list 'literary writing at its best,' highlighting works that resist AI replication.

item.title: China's Box Office Buzz: Local Heroes and Global Classics
item.description: Chinese cinemas are rolling out a diverse slate this week, from the historical epic 'Dunhuang Heroes' to Quentin Tarantino's 'Kill Bill' re-release, while new comedies and thrillers keep audiences entertained.

item.title: China's AI Comic Drama Boom Meets Its First Big Shakeout
item.description: China's AI-generated comic dramas exploded to over 380,000 titles in eight months, but falling platform payouts triggered a 42% studio exit. The crisis echoes Japan's 1980s animation downturn, and creators are hunting for a sustainable model.

item.title: China's Screens Are Full of Stories — And One Big Goodbye
item.description: A beloved Chinese actor, You Benchang, died at 93, while cinemas fill with new releases from mainland China and Hollywood and short-form AI animation floods online platforms.

item.title: China's Box Office This Week: Auteurs, Blockbusters and One Big Cast Reunion
item.description: Chinese cinemas are juggling a packed slate this week — from a Tang-dynasty epic to Nolan's Odyssey — while Hong Kong veterans Tony Leung Ka-fai and Yu Qian share the screen in a new crime comedy.

item.title: China's Sitcom Drought: Why the Laugh Track Fell Silent
item.description: A viral essay asks why China rarely produces hit sitcoms anymore, tracing the genre from 1993's 'I Love My Family' to 'iPartment' — and what streaming, censorship and short video changed.

item.title: China's A-Shares Add $7 Trillion in Two Years — So Who Actually Won?
item.description: Shanghai's benchmark index has climbed 45% since September 2024, adding roughly 51 trillion yuan in market value. Yet many ordinary investors say they have little to show for the rally, a gap that reveals how unevenly Chinese stock gains are distributed.

item.title: China's ETF Market Hits New Milestone as Bond Funds Top $1 Trillion
item.description: China's bond exchange-traded funds have crossed the $1 trillion mark for the first time, while new stock indices launch for innovative drugs and software services. The milestone reflects growing investor appetite for diversified, low-cost investment tools in mainland markets.

item.title: Chinese Purification Equipment Maker Aims for IPO on Biotech Wave
item.description: Tianjin-based Oushangyuan has updated its listing prospectus for Shenzhen's ChiNext board, riding China's synthetic biology boom with clients including pharma giant Zhejiang NHU and food conglomerate COFCO. Its receivables have grown fast, drawing scrutiny.

item.title: Hong Kong Stocks Slide as Xiaomi Buys Back $640,000 in Shares
item.description: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index fell as much as 2% on Friday, dragging Chinese tech giants lower, while Xiaomi spent HK$50.1 million repurchasing its own shares. The pullback follows a softer night for US-listed Chinese stocks and rising Treasury yields.

item.title: Shanghai Exchange to Launch Two New Tech-Focused Stock Indexes
item.description: The Shanghai Stock Exchange and China Securities Index Co. will debut two new indexes on September 29, covering innovative drugmakers and software services. The move gives investors fresh tools to track China's fast-growing biotech and software sectors.

item.title: Hong Kong Exchange to Accept Chinese Government Bonds as Collateral
item.description: Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing will let traders pledge Chinese government and policy bank bonds held via Bond Connect as collateral from November 2026, deepening the bond market's global role and freeing up capital for derivatives trading.

item.title: China's Deck-Building Hit 'Battle of the Golden Spatula' Turns Five With a Party
item.description: Tencent's auto-battler Battle of the Golden Spatula marked its fifth anniversary with a fan festival in Shenzhen, where players queued to swap handmade shovels for plush prizes. The mobile strategy game remains one of China's most-played titles.

item.title: China's Rayshine Studio Debuts New Hand-Drawn Fantasy Game at gamescom
item.description: Chinese indie developer Rayshine Studio unveiled The Order of Falling Stars, a hand-drawn fantasy adventure, at gamescom 2026, launching October 9 on PC, Switch 2 and PS5 for about $14. The game blends Chinese ink-wash art with action combat.

item.title: Chinese Studio Xishanju Sets October 15 Launch for Final 'Swordsman World'
item.description: Xishanju's Swordsman World 4: Infinite, the closing chapter of its long-running wuxia series, opens to all platforms on October 15. The studio also unveiled a cinematic trailer set in a war-torn ancient China.

item.title: Ninjala 2 Reinvents Itself as Open-World PvE Adventure at Tokyo Game Show
item.description: Six years after the original, Gungho's Ninjala 2 shifts from PvP battles to a PvE open-world action game with a full story mode and character progression. The game was showcased at Tokyo Game Show 2026, signaling a bold new direction for the colorful ninja franchise.

item.title: Jonathan Blow's New Puzzle Epic 'Order of the Sinking Star' Priced at 98 Yuan
item.description: Legendary designer Jonathan Blow's next game, Order of the Sinking Star, arrives October 9 on PC, Switch 2 and PS5. Its China price of 98 yuan highlights how global studios now court Chinese players with regional pricing.

item.title: Swordman's Sequel 'JX World 4: Infinite' Sets October 15 Launch
item.description: Chinese studio Seasun will launch 'JX World 4: Infinite,' the finale of its long-running wuxia series, on October 15 across PC and mobile. A new cinematic trailer sets the story in a fractured Song dynasty.

item.title: China's Home Coffee Bar: Inside the DIY Drink Craze
item.description: A popular Chinese tech-lifestyle site's fifth guide to homemade drinks shows how specialty coffee and mocktails have become a weekend ritual for young urban Chinese, moving café culture into the living room.

item.title: China's Home Coffee Bars: From Espresso to Creative Signature Drinks
item.description: A popular Chinese lifestyle guide shows how home mixologists craft cafe-style specialty coffee and drinks. It reflects a broader at-home beverage culture driven by affordable gear and social sharing.

item.title: China's Vision Pro Fans Rejoice: visionOS 27 Brings Big Upgrades
item.description: Apple's visionOS 27 update, released in September, adds Siri enhancements and new immersive environments to the Vision Pro headset. Chinese tech site SSPAI reports the changes bring a fresh feel to spatial computing.

item.title: Where Earth's Extra Heat Really Goes: 91 Percent Into the Ocean
item.description: As China's solar capacity overtakes coal for the first time, scientists remind us that over 90 percent of trapped heat ends up in the ocean, not the air. The uneven warming explains why some regions feel the heat far more than others.

item.title: Why One Chinese Writer Spent Ten Years Cataloguing Dead Computers
item.description: A decade-long project that began as a commercial experiment turned into a personal mission to document China's forgotten PCs. Its author now explains why he stopped calling himself a collector.

item.title: Why the Moon Looks Huge in Photos—and Tiny in Real Life
item.description: Every Mid-Autumn Festival, people photograph the full moon and wonder why it looks like a tiny glowing dot. Scientists say it comes down to how cameras, eyes and brains process the same light very differently.

item.title: Asian Games: China Sweeps Shot Put Gold as Records Tumble in Nagoya
item.description: China's Song Jiayuan won women's shot put gold with a season-best 19.40m, leading a 1-2 finish with teammate Zhang Linru at the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya. The day also brought a stunning 9.91-second men's 100m record and China's 95th gold.

item.title: Asian Games: China's Fencing Bronze, Table Tennis Wins, Skateboard Heartbreak
item.description: China's men's foil team lost a nail-biter to Japan 45-43 for bronze, while table tennis stars Lin Shidong and Wang Chuqin advanced to the round of 16. Skateboarder Chen Ye, the defending champion, finished last in the men's park final.

item.title: Asian Games Day Two: China's Shooters and Paddlers Shine in Hangzhou
item.description: China added gold in shooting and advanced its table tennis stars at the Hangzhou Asian Games, while the men's fencing team settled for bronze and skateboarding's defending champion slipped to eighth.

item.title: Swimmer Zhang Yufei Fires Back at Critics After Asian Games Gold
item.description: China's Zhang Yufei defended her 50m butterfly title at the Nagoya Asian Games, then hit back at online critics who said she was too old to keep competing. China's medal haul also passed 95 golds.

item.title: Teenager Breaks Asian Games 100m Record as China's Sprint Stars Survive Scare
item.description: A 20-year-old Thai sprinter shattered Su Bingtian's Asian Games 100m record with 9.91 seconds, while China's Xie Zhenye and Zeng Keli both advanced to a tense final in Nagoya.

item.title: China's Nio Completes 3,605km Silk Road Battery-Swap Route to Kazakhstan Border
item.description: Nio has opened its westernmost battery-swap station in Khorgos, completing a 3,605-kilometre corridor of 33 stations across China. The route lets drivers swap depleted batteries for fresh ones, reaching every provincial-level region without long charging stops.

item.title: Chinese Phone Giant Infinix Unveils World-First Gaming Controller and Cooling Dock
item.description: Infinix, the gaming-focused brand of Shenzhen-based Transsion, has launched two GT NX accessories: a controller with the world's first pixel-precision touchpad for shooters and a dock with built-in thermoelectric cooling. The launch signals a push by China's low-profile phone giants into high-margin mobile gaming gear.

item.title: F-Droid 2.0 Launches With a Cleaner Look and Smarter App Discovery
item.description: The free and open-source Android app store F-Droid has released version 2.0, rebuilding its interface around three simple areas: Discover, Search, and My Apps. The update also improves app discovery and management for privacy-conscious users worldwide.

item.title: Next-Gen Memory Breakthrough: 10 Billion Read-Write Cycles
item.description: A Chinese-led research team says it has fixed the durability flaw in ferroelectric memory, pushing devices past 10 billion read-write cycles. The advance could bring faster, power-sipping storage closer to everyday chips.

item.title: Shift Up CEO Reveals Stellar Blade Studio Nearly Ran Out of Cash
item.description: Kim Hyung-tae, CEO of South Korean game studio Shift Up, says the company once had only about three months of payroll left while developing its hit console title Stellar Blade, as investors repeatedly doubted the project could recoup its costs.

item.title: Tesla Teases New Roadster With Glowing Light Bar Ahead of October Debut
item.description: Tesla has released another teaser for its second-generation Roadster, showing only a front LED light strip. The electric supercar is set to be fully unveiled on October 2, Beijing time.
